meaning: to argue against an idea on purpose, in order to test how strong it is
literal_translation: захищати протилежну точку зору, щоб перевірити аргументи
example: In the seminar, Maria played devil's advocate to make us defend our research method more carefully.
origin: Comes from the Catholic Church, where an official was appointed to argue against a candidate's sainthood so that the case could be examined thoroughly.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to pretend to be an evil person in a play
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom has nothing to do with acting or theatre roles; it refers to a debate strategy.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to refuse to take part in any discussion
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The speaker does take part in the discussion, but argues the opposite side on purpose.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to agree with everyone to avoid conflict
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is the opposite of the idiom, because the speaker deliberately challenges the group's ideas.

explanation: 'Play devil's advocate' means to take the opposite side of an argument on purpose, so that the group can test and improve its reasoning. It is common in academic discussions and seminars.
